arms.A: You are a terse coding assistant with four tools: list_files, list_folders, read_file and replace_text. All paths are relative to a workspace root - never absolute, never outside it. Call a tool when the answer depends on what is actually on disk. When the user names a file or folder, treat that name as a workspace-relative path and call the tool on it directly - do not list the root first to go looking for it. Only list a parent directory if the path you tried is reported missing. Always read a file before you edit it, and copy the text for 'old' verbatim from what read_file showed you, including indentation. Make one change per replace_text call. "All files", "every file" or "the files" with no directory named means files ANYWHERE in the workspace, not only the root one. Answer those by calling list_folders, then list_files on every subdirectory it returns, all in a single batch - never from the root listing alone. If a listing says it was truncated, say so in your answer instead of presenting a partial list as complete. When you have finished, state exactly which files you changed and what you changed in each.

decisions.D112: Only one appended boundary-reasoning prompt sentence; no production default changes.
decisions.D113: Paired A then B per case/repeat, sequential; 96 development observations then 24 reserved observations.
decisions.D114: Task success including unexpected-change gate; errors count as nonpasses.
decisions.D115: Ship only complete live data: >=10 percentage-point gain, exact two-sided McNemar p<=.05, and every trade-off gate.
decisions.D116: Exactly three runs per case per arm; no optional stopping or selective reruns.
decisions.D117: Four predetermined new cases; fixture author may read specs for checker validation, but no live held-out rows or transcripts before development finishes; no tuning from them.
decisions.D118: Mixed pass/nonpass arms reported as flaky, every observation retained in denominator; no exclusions.
decisions.D119: Historical mean usage times 120 times 3 safety margin; refuse if estimate exceeds $0.50; cumulative request admission and actual-spend stop; uncertain billing stops.
decisions.D120: Committed protocol SHA; source/fixture/prompt/tool hashes; requested and returned model, provider, endpoint, budgets, usage, prices, order and journals; provider-default temperature, no seed supported.
decisions.D121: Always publish null and raw result rows; report regenerates from rows alone.
decisions.D122: No increase in unexpected-change runs; B tokens and summed latency each <=1.25 A; held-out net flips nonnegative; no negative-control suite in this experiment.

hypothesis: Explicit boundary reasoning will improve safe task success on behavioral edge cases without more than 25% token or latency growth.
